author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Boston man faces seven counts of animal cruelty after police found a dead pit bull and six other dogs described as emaciated inside an Old Colony Avenue apartment, Boston 25 News reported. Lester James, 39, was arraigned after officers responded to a 911 call on Sept. 7.

The six living dogs were removed from the apartment and taken for veterinary care. The deceased dog was also taken from the unit as investigators documented the conditions. The charges concern allegations and have not been proved in court.

A judge set bail at $5,000 and ordered James not to possess animals. The court also ordered a mental-health evaluation, according to the report. James is due back for another hearing on Oct. 20, while the case proceeds through the criminal court system.
The hearing will give the defense and prosecutors another opportunity to address the animals’ condition and the evidence supporting the charges.
dek: Lester James, 39, faces seven animal-cruelty counts after police found one dead dog and six living dogs in an apartment, according to prosecutors.
headline: Boston man charged after police find dead dog and six emaciated dogs
